title: Opslet SDK and runtime-safe-executor for idempotent admin utilities
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight SDK (opslet) and a 'runtime-safe-executor' that composes verified runbook steps into idempotent, auditable micro-operations. The opslet SDK should let engineers register step templates, define inputs/outputs, and emit typed telemetry. The runtime-safe-executor enforces RBAC, dry-run, KMS-encrypted secrets access, and automatic rollback hooks for partial failures. This reduces on-call cognitive load by enabling short, repeatable admin actions with traceable provenance.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Opslet SDK published to internal PyPI and npm with docs; 2) Runtime enforces RBAC and logs audit entries for each step; 3) Dry-run mode simulates changes without side effects; 4) At least two production runbooks converted and validated; 5) End-to-end telemetry visible in Console per-route breakdown.
implementation_notes: - Language: initial PoC Python, follow-up TypeScript SDK for frontend tooling. - Runtime integrates with admin-proxy service (service account model) and Console tracing. - Use prefix/KV cache patterns from runtime team to avoid repeated long RPCs when composing steps. - Telemetry: token-level timing, step success/failure reasons, replay-id for audits. - Secrets: fetch via KMS/HSM integration with short-lived tokens. - Rollout plan: feature-flagged per-team, start with support-org.
tradeoffs: - Building SDK vs. templating DSL: SDK provides typed safety and easier testing but increases onboarding. - Synchronous enforcement increases latency for shortflows; mitigate with async status polling and optimistic dry-run.
risks: - Privilege escalation if RBAC misconfigured; mitigated by principle-of-least-privilege defaults and separate audit reviewer flow. - Incorrect idempotency semantics on third-party ops; include explicit compensating actions template.
notes: Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood/internals/opslet-sdk; PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821. Testing plan includes simulated incident replay harness and service-level chaos tests.
